author_or_org: Vahid Majdinasab, Michael Joshua Bishop, Shawn Rasheed, Arghavan Moradidakhel, Amjed Tahir, Foutse Khomh

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The abstract states that AI-powered code generation models allow developers to expedite code generation and thereby improve productivity.
claims.quote: AI-powered code generation models have been developing rapidly, allowing developers to expedite code generation and thus improve their productivity.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The paper is a targeted replication of Pearce et al.'s Copilot security study using newer versions of Copilot and CodeQL, focused on Python code.
claims.quote: This paper replicates the study of Pearce et al., which investigated security weaknesses in Copilot and uncovered several weaknesses in the code suggested by Copilot across diverse scenarios and languages (Python, C and Verilog). Our replication examines Copilot security weaknesses using newer versions of Copilot and CodeQL (the security analysis framework). The replication focused on the presence of security vulnerabilities in Python code.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The percentage of vulnerable code suggestions fell from 36.54% to 27.25%, but newer Copilot versions still suggested insecure code.
claims.quote: Our results indicate that, even with the improvements in newer versions of Copilot, the percentage of vulnerable code suggestions has reduced from 36.54% to 27.25%. Nonetheless, it remains evident that the model still suggests insecure code.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Recent studies found security weaknesses in code generated by AI tools including GitHub Copilot and Amazon CodeWhisperer.
claims.quote: Recent studies have investigated security issues in AI-powered code generation tools such as GitHub Copilot and Amazon CodeWhisperer, revealing several security weaknesses in the code generated by these tools.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Code generation models are trained on large public-repository code corpora that may contain bugs and vulnerabilities.
claims.quote: These models are trained on large corpora of code (primarily sourced from public repositories), which may contain bugs and vulnerabilities.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The source notes that concerns have been raised about the security of code generated by these models.
claims.quote: Several concerns have been raised about the security of the code generated by these models.
